src: 言いたいことは分かる
ja: 言いたいことは分かる
kana: いいたいことはわかる
politeJa: 言いたいことは分かります
english: I see what you're getting at (but ...); I get your point
use: Acknowledges someone's point before disagreeing; a kedo usually follows.

example.romaji: iitai koto wa wakaru kedo, chotto kibishii yo.
example.ja: 言いたいことは分かるけど、ちょっと厳しいよ。
example.english: I get your point, but that's a bit harsh.

examplePolite.romaji: iitai koto wa wakarimasu kedo, jikan ga arimasen.
examplePolite.ja: 言いたいことは分かりますけど、時間がありません。
examplePolite.english: I see your point, but we don't have time.

notes: The wa means 'that much I get', so it rarely signals full agreement.

kana: かんがえたことなかった
politeJa: 考えたことなかったです
english: I'd never thought about that; that never occurred to me
use: Reacts with real surprise to a new angle or question, often after e or naruhodo.

example.romaji: e, sou ka. sonna no kangaeta koto nakatta.
example.ja: え、そうか。そんなの考えたことなかった。
example.english: Oh, right. I'd never thought about that.

examplePolite.romaji: naruhodo, sore wa kangaeta koto nakatta desu.
examplePolite.ja: なるほど、それは考えたことなかったです。
examplePolite.english: I see, I'd never thought of that.

notes: -ta koto nai means 'have never ...': itta koto nai (I've never been).

kana: むずかしいところだね
english: that's a tough one; it's a tricky question
use: Buys time or avoids taking sides on a hard choice; also a soft no to a request.

example.romaji: dotchi mo ii kara, muzukashii tokoro da ne.
example.ja: どっちもいいから、難しいところだね。
example.english: They're both good, so that's a tough one.

examplePolite.romaji: sore wa muzukashii tokoro desu ne.
examplePolite.ja: それは難しいところですね。

notes: At work, muzukashii (it's difficult) often means no.

src: そういう考え方もあるね
ja: そういう考え方もあるね
kana: そういうかんがえかたもあるね
romaji: sou iu kangaekata mo aru ne
polite: sou iu kangaekata mo arimasu ne
politeJa: そういう考え方もありますね
english: that's one way to look at it; fair point
use: Accepts another view as valid without fully agreeing; useful to cool a debate.

example.romaji: naruhodo ne. sou iu kangaekata mo aru ne.
example.ja: なるほどね。そういう考え方もあるね。
example.english: I see. That's one way to look at it.

examplePolite.romaji: naruhodo, sou iu kangaekata mo arimasu ne.
examplePolite.ja: なるほど、そういう考え方もありますね。
examplePolite.english: I see, that's one way to look at it.

notes: The mo (also) keeps your own view standing; a flat tone can sound dismissive.

english: I'm not so sure about ...; I have my doubts about ...
use: Indirect criticism of a choice or behaviour; it sounds mild but clearly means you disapprove.

example.romaji: kaigi de sore iu no wa, dou ka to omou yo.
example.ja: 会議でそれ言うのは、どうかと思うよ。
example.english: I'm not sure saying that in a meeting is a good idea.

examplePolite.romaji: sono iikata wa, chotto dou ka to omoimasu.
examplePolite.ja: その言い方は、ちょっとどうかと思います。
examplePolite.english: I have my doubts about putting it that way.

notes: Not a question despite dou ka; chotto before it softens it further.

english: I mean, it's fine, but ...; whatever, fine
use: Agrees while hinting you're not thrilled; tone decides whether it sounds relaxed or sulky.

example.romaji: betsu ni ii kedo, tsugi wa saki ni itte ne.
example.ja: 別にいいけど、次は先に言ってね。
example.english: It's fine, but tell me first next time.

examplePolite.romaji: betsu ni ii desu kedo, tsugi wa oshiete kudasai ne.
examplePolite.ja: 別にいいですけど、次は教えてくださいね。
examplePolite.english: It's fine, but please let me know next time.

notes: Betsu ni alone ('not really', 'nothing') can sound cold.

romaji: ... tte iu hito mo iru kedo
polite: ... to iu hito mo imasu kedo
use: Brings up another view so you can disagree with it without owning it.

example.romaji: takai tte iu hito mo iru kedo, watashi wa yasui to omou.
example.ja: 高いって言う人もいるけど、私は安いと思う。
example.english: Some say it's pricey, but I think it's cheap.

examplePolite.romaji: fuben da to iu hito mo imasu kedo, watashi wa suki desu.
examplePolite.ja: 不便だと言う人もいますけど、私は好きです。
examplePolite.english: Some people say it's inconvenient, but I like it.

notes: Tte is the casual form of the quoting to.

src: 偏見かもしれないけど
ja: 偏見かもしれないけど
kana: へんけんかもしれないけど
politeJa: 偏見かもしれませんけど
english: this might be a stereotype, but ...; maybe I'm biased, but ...
use: Softens a generalisation about a group or place before you say it.

example.romaji: henken kamo shirenai kedo, oosaka no hito tte omoshiroi yo ne.
example.ja: 偏見かもしれないけど、大阪の人って面白いよね。
example.english: Maybe it's a stereotype, but people from Osaka are funny, right?

examplePolite.romaji: henken kamo shiremasen kedo, toukyou no hito wa aruku no ga hayai desu ne.
examplePolite.ja: 偏見かもしれませんけど、東京の人は歩くのが速いですね。
examplePolite.english: Maybe it's a stereotype, but people in Tokyo walk fast.

notes: Henken means 'prejudice'; kamo shirenai (might be) is often shortened to kamo.
